title: In Deuteronomy 6 How Can We Effectively Teach The Values Of Our Faith To The Next Generation
paragraphs: Passing the Baton: Teaching the Values of Faith from Deuteronomy 6

Deuteronomy 6 stands as one of the foundational chapters for understanding how the people of God are to pass their faith from one generation to the next. It not only offers instruction but also reveals God’s heart for families, communities, and the future of faith.
The Heart of Deuteronomy 6: Love and Obedience
The chapter begins with Moses reminding Israel of the importance of obeying God’s commands so that they and their children may prosper:

Now this is the commandment, the statutes, and the ordinances, which Jehovah your God commanded to teach you... that thou mightest fear Jehovah thy God, to keep all his statutes and his commandments... thou, and thy son, and thy son’s son. - Deuteronomy 6:1-2 ASV
The faith is not just about personal obedience, but about multi-generational faithfulness.
The Shema: The Foundation of Biblical Parenting
At the heart of Deuteronomy 6 is the Shema—a declaration of God’s uniqueness and a call to wholehearted love:
Hear, O Israel: Jehovah our God is one Jehovah: and thou shalt love Jehovah thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might. - Deuteronomy 6:4-5 ASV
Jesus later affirmed this as the greatest commandment (Matthew 22:37 ASV), underscoring its centrality. The primary value we must teach the next generation is a love for God above all.
How Do We Teach Our Faith?
The passage gives clear guidance on transmitting faith:

And these words, which I command thee this day, shall be upon thy heart; and thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thy house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up. - Deuteronomy 6:6-7 ASV
Internalize God’s Word: The commands must first be “upon your heart.” We cannot pass on what we do not possess. Personal devotion is foundational.
Diligent Teaching: The instruction to “teach them diligently” implies intentionality and effort. Faith is not absorbed by accident; it requires purposeful instruction.

Everyday Conversations: Teaching happens “when you sit...walk...lie down...rise up.” The home is the primary place of discipleship, and faith discussions should be woven into the fabric of daily life.
Practical Methods for Today
Modeling Faith: Children learn most by example. As Paul wrote, Be ye imitators of me, even as I also am of Christ. - 1 Corinthians 11:1 ASV

Scripture Memorization: The Israelites were told to bind God’s words “as a sign upon thy hand...between thine eyes” (Deuteronomy 6:8 ASV). Today, this might mean posting verses in your home or memorizing together as a family.

Storytelling: When children ask, “What mean the testimonies...?” (see Deuteronomy 6:20 ASV), parents are to recount God’s faithfulness. Our stories of God’s work in our lives are powerful teaching tools.
Gospel Centrality
The ultimate value to pass on is the message of God’s grace. The law points us to our need for Christ. As Paul wrote,
So that the law is become our tutor to bring us unto Christ, that we might be justified by faith. - Galatians 3:24 ASV
While we teach moral values, we must emphasize salvation by grace through faith in Jesus Christ (Ephesians 2:8-9 ASV).
A Warning and a Promise
Deuteronomy 6 warns against forgetting God in times of prosperity:
Then beware lest thou forget Jehovah, who brought thee forth out of the land of Egypt... - Deuteronomy 6:12 ASV
Each generation must be vigilant to remember and rehearse God’s mighty acts, so faith does not become stale tradition.
Conclusion: The Mission Continues

Teaching the next generation is not just a duty but a privilege. As we love God wholeheartedly, immerse ourselves in His Word, and intentionally disciple those who come after us, we join God’s great plan of redemption across the ages.
